component.name: Soyuz
component.summary: Keyboard-first file manager that never blocks

description.p: Soyuz is a file manager built around one promise: the window never stops responding. Every copy, move, delete, extract or checksum runs as a background job with real progress, pause, resume and cancel, conflict handling, history and undo.

ul.li: Tabs, dual panes and workspaces, all driven from the keyboard and a command palette
Background jobs with undo; deletes go to the trash first
Previews for images, text, code, audio and archives, plus Quick Look
Streaming search, folder sizes, a treemap, duplicate finder and folder compare
Browse and create zip, tar and 7z archives
An embedded terminal and remote locations over SFTP, WebDAV, FTP and S3
One TOML file configures everything, editable from the Settings window

description.p: SQLite is updated for a security fix in the bundled library, and rustix for a memory-safety fix. This is also the first release that Soyuz 0.8.0 can install by itself with Update and restart.

Soyuz checks for a new version once a day and installs it in one click: Update and restart downloads the release, checks it against the release's checksums, installs it and starts Soyuz again. Nothing is downloaded before the click, and the check can be switched off in Settings.

The command palette starts the applications installed on the computer: type part of an app's name, or start with ! to list only apps. Each app shows its own icon. On Windows this includes Store apps such as Paint, Calculator and Terminal.

The terminal system monitor now draws its boxes, graphs and meters in the style of btop. Live graphs draw at once after a restart or a stopped recording, chart hover cards are no longer cut off by small charts, and the smart folders section shows in the sidebar while the index is off, with a hint to turn it on.

The system monitor now works in every window. Before, a monitor tab in any window but the main one said "No readings yet", and it lost its filter and selection, until the main window showed the monitor too.

Operations of the same kind now share one notification. It counts them while they run and ends with one Undo for the whole group, so deleting files one by one no longer leaves a queue of notifications behind. Failures stay visible as a warning. Merging can be turned off in Settings.

Fixes for working with several windows. Dragging a folder to another Soyuz window now moves or copies it like a drag between panes, instead of sending the original to the trash. A menu or dropdown in one window no longer stops every keyboard shortcut in windows opened later. A window opened from the file manager gets the keyboard, and a dialog waiting in another window comes to the front when you press a key.

Sharper text: LCD subpixel smoothing by default, with normal hinting and a softer text colour in the Orbit themes. Text smoothing is a new setting (LCD, LCD with reversed stripes, or Grayscale), and GPUs without per-channel blending stay on Grayscale. Settings that still held the old defaults move to the new ones.

System monitor, in a tab of the window and of the terminal UI: processes as a list or a tree with your own columns and text, regular expression and column filters; CPU, memory, disk, network, GPU and sensor graphs; open connections, services and startup programs; optional recorded history, snapshots and comparisons; alerts. Also: quieter scrollbars, and filter and search fields center their text.

Security update: zip, russh and pageant are updated for published advisories, including a critical one in zip archive handling. When the item under the cursor is deleted, the cursor now moves to the next item, or the previous one at the end of the list (Settings, Behaviour, After deleting).

The 0.5.10 changes, built: its release stopped on Linux test failures and a download outage. Also on Linux, undo of a move or rename no longer takes a new file that reused the old one's inode for the file it moved.

Open with gets a program browser and remembers what you pick. Text size now reaches every surface, figures line up with a tabular cut of Inter, and long names keep what matters when cut. Natural sort of large folders is about 16 times faster. Fixes for data safety: Enter on a focused Cancel no longer confirms a dialog, a config file that does not load is never overwritten, and copying a link keeps the old file until the link exists.

Text and code previews use the Hack font at a larger size and follow the code font size setting. The activity history can be cleared, and Delete moves files to the trash without asking (it can be undone). The window no longer freezes when a job with thousands of items finishes.
The 0.5.7 changes, built: that release's build stopped on a test that only failed on Linux. Also updates the zstd compression library for two security advisories.

Programs that need administrator rights (most installers) open again, with the system's permission prompt, and the context menu offers Run as administrator (Run as root on Linux). The right-click menu is much shorter: a row of quick action buttons, related entries in submenus, entries for the file's type first, colour tags as a row of dots, and rarely used entries under More (Shift+right-click shows everything). All of it is configurable. Shift+F10 opens the menu from the keyboard.
Build fix: a source comment no longer trips the check that keeps Windows shell APIs out of Soyuz. No functional changes.

Folders opened from the file manager while Soyuz is minimized open at once, files can be dragged out of every Soyuz window into other apps again, and a minimized main window no longer keeps redrawing.
Programs show their own icons in every file view, read directly from the program file.
Security fix: the SMB client and the SSH key code use updated cryptography crates that close timing side channels (RUSTSEC-2026-0385, RUSTSEC-2026-0387).

Every Soyuz window runs in one process and uses much less memory. Panels docked on the right no longer squeeze the file list below a configurable width. HTML files and web links open correctly in Chrome and Edge on Windows, and Ctrl+click on a web link in the terminal opens the browser.

Files whose default app is a Microsoft Store app, such as photos opening in Photos, open on double-click again on Windows, and Store apps with a command alias (Paint, Notepad, Media Player) appear in Open with. FFmpeg load errors say why the libraries could not be loaded.

Tar and 7z archives can be edited like zip archives, and files can be copied out of any archive, including archives inside archives. Quick share serves files over the local network with a QR code. Drive cards show disk health (SMART / NVMe). Compare as treemap shows how two folders differ. Copies clone or link duplicate files where the volume allows. Content search looks inside PDFs. Also: "Why is this slow?" in job details, servers found on the local network, CAB sets and spanned zips, WebDAV Digest sign-in, clipboard history, folder notes, focus mode, plain-language requests to the assistant with editable plans, and journal catch-up without administrator rights.

System folders such as AppData, ProgramData and Temp on Windows, and ~/.config, ~/.local/share, ~/.cache and /tmp on Linux, appear below the favorites after a System divider that hides them; Settings picks which ones show.

Ctrl+C and Ctrl+V in the address bar, rename fields and other text now use the system clipboard, pasting a copied picture saves it as a PNG file again, and every folder listing ends with blank space to right-click for New folder and Paste. Executable programs and AppImages start on Enter or double-click.

Built on egui 0.37: colour emoji, kinetic scrolling with rubber-banding, and pasting a copied picture saves it as a PNG file. Files no application is registered for (and files without an extension) open with Open with…, which can remember the choice.
Default apps per file type inside Soyuz (Open with… remembers the last app and can make it the default; Shift+Enter opens it), and a play / pause key (P) for Quick Look.

Media through the FFmpeg libraries, loaded at run time and shipped with the app: video playback in the preview pane, Quick Look and the terminal UI, thumbnails and previews for more formats, media tools (convert, extract audio, trim, save frame) as undoable jobs, the same tools for the AI assistant, MCP clients and scripts, hardware video decoding, and an in-app download of the FFmpeg runtime.
Fixes to the test suite on Linux and Windows; the app itself is unchanged from 0.3.1.
The assistant's folder scope accepts paths written with short (8.3) names or through junctions.
The terminal UI (soyuz --tui) reaches feature parity with the window and gains a screen-reader mode; saves on Windows no longer get lost when another program has the file open.
Stability fixes; About shows the git commit the build comes from.
First public build. Linux packages are new and less tested than the Windows build.
